dod_intent_evidence: Air Force SBIR Phase III IDIQ (August 2025) for protecting tactical-edge communications including airborne WANs, air-to-air links, and mobile ad-hoc networks supporting Agile Combat Employment, plus a USCYBERCOM red-team exercise validation — News section and homepage testimonial.
score_evidence: 'Compliance certified — FIPS-140 and NSA/NIST post-quantum guidelines' -> deployment_awareness_absence: compliance is framed entirely in civilian NIST/FIPS terms; ATO, RMF, CMMC, and IL4/IL5 never appear once despite the company now selling onto DoD tactical networks

Testimonials come from an 'International Telecom Executive,' 'USCYBERCOM Exercise Chief,' 'Major US Utility Senior Network Administrator,' and 'Power Industry Consortium Principal Cybersecurity Manager' -> operator_absence: every named validator is a civilian/enterprise administrator; no warfighter or tactical operator voice appears anywhere despite the new airborne/MANET contract

'Q-Net Security Secures a SBIR Phase III IDIQ Contract with the U.S. Air Force to Protect Tactical Edge Communications' (Aug 2025) at a 13-person, decade-old (2015) Series A company -> stage_pressure: a small team just took on a materially new domain (airborne WANs, air-to-air links, MANET, ACE) via an IDIQ that guarantees no task orders

blind_spots.blind_spot: The Q-Box is validated as a 'bump-in-the-wire' device for fixed infrastructure (power grid PLC/RTU/sensors), but nothing in the pack addresses size, weight, or power for an airborne WAN or air-to-air link platform — a fundamentally different SWaP-C envelope.
blind_spots.operator_reality: A device sized and powered for a substation cabinet is not automatically sized and powered for an aircraft or a MANET radio pack; without published evidence of ruggedization or power-envelope work for the new tactical-edge contract, the jump from 'utility bump-in-the-wire' to 'airborne WAN' is unaddressed engineering risk hiding behind reused marketing language.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Every product claim and testimonial in the pack (power grid, telecom, USCYBERCOM smart-city exercise) validates the fixed-infrastructure use case; none validate the airborne/tactical-edge use case the Air Force contract just added.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: A silicon encryption device — no processor, no OS, no software — that drops directly in line on the ethernet segment of the device it protects.

blind_spots.blind_spot: All five customer testimonials are civilian or enterprise administrators — none are military operators — despite the company just winning a tactical-edge Air Force contract covering airborne WANs and mobile ad-hoc networks.
blind_spots.operator_reality: A 'set and forget' pitch that lands well with a fixed power-grid administrator may face a completely different adoption story with an aircrew or ground MANET operator who has to trust the device under EW conditions and combat tempo — the pack shows no evidence Q-Net has yet gathered or published that operator-level validation for the new domain.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The Phase III IDIQ was only announced in August 2025; the public testimonial set still reflects the company's original critical-infrastructure/enterprise customer base rather than the new DoD tactical-edge use case.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: The gear we have in place at the plant is still operational and has been working properly without issue. — Major US Utility Senior Network Administrator

blind_spots.blind_spot: Compliance claims are framed entirely as FIPS-140 and NSA/NIST post-quantum guidance — civilian cryptographic certification — with zero mention of ATO, RMF, CMMC, or IL4/IL5 anywhere in the pack, even as the company moves onto DoD tactical networks.
blind_spots.operator_reality: FIPS-140 certification proves the crypto module itself is sound; it does not grant an Authority to Operate on a DoD network or an Agile Combat Employment communications architecture. Treating NIST/FIPS certification as sufficient for DoD fielding is a common Valley-of-Death misstep, and nothing in the pack shows the RMF/ATO conversation has started.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The company's compliance messaging was built for its original enterprise/critical-infrastructure buyers, where FIPS-140 and NIST guidance are the relevant bar — that messaging hasn't yet been updated for a DoD-network buyer where ATO/RMF is the actual gate.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Unmatched cybersecurity ... Compliance certified — FIPS-140 and NSA/NIST post-quantum guidelines.

opener_hook: Every customer quote on your site is a telecom executive or a utility network administrator — your new Air Force Phase III covers airborne WANs and MANET, and there's no operator-level validation story for that domain on the page yet.
what_they_do: Silicon-based, processor-less hardware encryption device (Q-Box) that bump-in-the-wire protects point-to-point network links, proven in utility/critical-infrastructure and telecom deployments, now transitioning via an Air Force SBIR Phase III IDIQ into protecting tactical-edge communications (airborne WANs, air-to-air links, MANET).
